root_cause.text: Using `event->pmu` instead of `pmu_ctx->pmu` when cloning events during inheritance and when performing group reads, causing a mismatch between the PMU context and the actual PMU used by the event, which leads to wrong transaction handlers being invoked during group rollback and results in an out-of-bounds memory access in `x86_pmu_del()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `inherit_event()` to use `parent_event->pmu_ctx->pmu` instead of `parent_event->pmu`, and `__perf_event_read()` to use `event->pmu_ctx->pmu` instead of `event->pmu`. The CVE description explicitly states that "inherit uses event->pmu to clone the events, effectively undoing the move_group case for all inherited contexts." The resulting misuse of transaction handlers leads to the reported out-of-bounds access.
